Until the hats come off'). Speaker 'Mister Sable' = ORIGINAL+flag — canon members verified (Wilovan, Ratici, Crimshaw, Normen, Alcaz) but Wilovan is a GNOLL and the staging profile pins a HUMAN in a bowler; see brothers_lieutenant.md. hub.speaker: Mister Sable
hub.text: Begging your pardon, sir — a moment of your evening. We don't steal, whatever you've heard. We RECOVER. Occasionally we recover things that were never lost. Tonight we'd like to recover a man's good name — his, and by unfortunate arithmetic, ours.

text_variants.text: Evening, sir. The city's ears are long and the night is short — how goes our small disagreement?
Sir. The parlor door is never shut to you, the alleys are safe as churches — safer, we keep better hours — and a man remembers. All of us remember.

options.text: Remind me of the three doors.
Coyle's answered for it. Farley's name is clear.

commission.speaker: Mister Sable
commission.text: A merchant of standing, sir — Master Coyle, of Coyle and Sons, though the sons are decorative. He commissioned a quiet removal of certain goods. The removal went exactly as paid for. The ARREST afterward did not: our Mister Farley sits in a Watch cell for a theft he was hired to perform by the man now weeping loudest about it. We apologize in advance for imposing, sir. The Brothers cannot abide a frame. It's untidy.

why_you.speaker: Mister Sable
why_you.text: Because you're not us, sir — that's the whole of your qualification, and we mean it as flattery. Every hand in this brotherhood is known to the Watch by its glove size. A stranger's word lands where ours bounces. Also, and we say this with affection: you look like a person things HAPPEN to. We'd like to point you at Master Coyle and observe.

ways.speaker: Mister Sable
ways.text: Three doors, sir, as a man might put it. PAPER: Coyle keeps his true ledger at the counting-house off Wister's Alley, and paper doesn't lie — his says he paid for the theft himself. TONGUES: the fixer called Cups pours rumor by the alley gate, and Coyle has soured more partners than tea has leaves; testimony can be arranged. Politely arranged. Or FISTS — his warehouse crew — and we apologize for even setting that on the table, though should you open that particular door, sir, a man would be honored to attend.

marker.speaker: Mister Sable
marker.text: So we heard, sir. Mister Farley walked out this morning, hat restored to him at the gate — a small ceremony, but ours.

text_variants.text: So we heard, sir — the criers had it by breakfast and the Merchant's Guild by lunch. Coyle's name is now worth precisely what he paid for ours: nothing. Tidy. Mister Farley walked at dawn, and every hat on the street came off as he passed. Not for violence, sir. For respect. It confuses newcomers.

Quietly withdrawn, sir, charges and all — and a man notices your purse rides heavier than it did. We don't judge. We ADMIRE, on occasion, and this is one of those occasions. Do mind he stays bought; gentlemen of Coyle's sort un-buy themselves the moment it's cheap to.

marker_terms.speaker: Mister Sable
marker_terms.text: A Brother's marker, sir. Wood and tin, and worth rather more than its materials. Shown in the alleys, trouble will beg your pardon and step around you. Shown at the parlor, a man can find you things the shops pretend not to stock — recovered things, sir, of impeccable provenance. Which is to say: don't ask, and we shan't tell.

options.text: A pleasure doing business, Mister Sable.
